exposure: Prenatal exposure to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS)
outcome: Child neurodevelopment (autism spectrum disorder, typical development, non-typical development classification)
cohort: The study included 172 mother-child pairs from the MARBLES cohort, whose children were clinically classified at age three as having autism spectrum disorder (ASD), typical development (TD), or non-typical development (non-TD).
finding: Prenatal PFAS exposure was associated with maternal metabolic alterations, but no clear linkage to child neurodevelopment was observed.
